title: fix(husky): lock and scan failhides in the timestamps and secrets hooks
description:
found by the peer review of ehmpathy/rhachet beav/fix-clone-say-labeled-rule (the boot's declapract upgrade stamped these files). each is in practices/husky/best-practice/.

1. check.timestamps.lock.sh: an empty index read passes. after git rm --cached .husky/check.timestamps.sh the file stays on disk (hash-object still matches) and git ls-files -s prints naught, so the [ -z INDEX ] test short-circuits to a pass. fix: halt when the index read is empty.
2. check.timestamps.lock.sh: the TIMESTAMPS_LOCK_DISK git hash-object read is unguarded, so a git fault reads as a hook edit (ConstraintError) or aborts with git's code. fix: append || timestamps_lock_malfunction, as the index read already does.
3. check.timestamps.sh and check.secrets.sh: the scan pipelines end in head/cut with no pipefail, so a sed/grep fault (exit 2) reads as clean and the commit passes. fix: set -o pipefail, or check the grep status.
4. check.secrets.sh: the openai shape sk-(proj-)? matches an sk-ant- key before the anthropic shape, so an anthropic key is named openai-style. fix: order anthropic first, or exclude ant- in the openai pattern.
5. check.secrets.sh: no test of the shape matcher or its two halt messages. add fixture tests beside demo-repo-with-edited-timestamp-hook.
6. check.timestamps.sh header: drop the rhetorical tail (one dir today, every dir tomorrow); the directive above it already states the guard.
